transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: If I don't get home, leave the lane open for the next one. That's the job. There isn't a second part.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The frigate captain was at his wing ceremony. Half this coast was. The Marshal forgot that we all remember.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Green beacon. I'll stay close enough to read it.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: And then the Marshal answered. Fire at the orchard. A line of guns along the rivers.

transcript.speaker: RUSK
transcript.text: Varda Rim has broadcast enemy propaganda. It is a hostile station. The Teklan orchard sheltered the source. There will be no further warnings.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The orchard burned at noon. The old woman is alive. Her granddaughter is alive. The seed tin is ash. That's my report, and I hate it.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: I asked you to broadcast. I'd ask again. I need you to know that I'd ask again.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: The rain has passed. The line hasn't. I'll take the valleys.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The old woman heard Teal in her kitchen before the fire. She says he sounded tired. Now her neighbours are flying out over his saddle.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Teal flew that saddle on his checkride. Vulture Two signed the card. I pulled it last night. The handwriting matches the forged orders.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Two civilian airliners. One cannot climb. Somebody will have to leave the high sky to keep the lower one safe.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Then I'll fly his checkride for him. Properly, this time.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The eight towers in that crater are the Marshal's command array. The antennas up there are his. So is the pilot waiting above them.

transcript.speaker: VULTURE TWO
transcript.text: Varda trainee, this is Vulture Two. I taught your instructor to fly. I know what he'd try over that crater. Turn home. Nobody has to watch.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Vulture Two taught me that an order is not the same as a duty. Then he forgot. If you meet him, remind him. Loudly.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: He's challenged your call sign in daylight. He wants you above the crater, where he can see your face.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: If he ejects, mark where he lands. We need a witness who can answer back.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Then he'll see it.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Vulture Two ejected. Marines lifted him out of the crater. He asked if you were Teal's. I said yes.

transcript.speaker: VULTURE TWO
transcript.text: He was the best I ever signed off. Tell the kid the handwriting was mine. All of it. I'm done lying to pilots.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: I made a paper copy. Radios get jammed. Ink still travels. It's in the harbour master's safe, and she doesn't like the Marshal either.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The harbour master's copy and Vulture Two's statement are on one slow plane. Airships are jamming the ravine. Fighters are waiting beyond it.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The signatures, his tapes, a living witness on paper. If that plane falls, command gets to call him a deserter again.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Then it doesn't fall.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The evidence plane is clear. Its papers point to the crown station on the ice coast. Missiles are closing on the dish; we need its archive intact.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: At the crown station I left the order that started all of this. The first one. With his real signature, before he learned to use dead men's names.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: I didn't take it with me. I didn't trust myself to get home. I trusted the dish.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: He didn't trust himself to get home. He said it out loud, to a tape, and flew anyway. I keep rewinding that part.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: He trusted the dish. I can do that much.

transcript.speaker: LOG
transcript.text: ARCHIVE RECOVERED. ORDER 0001. 'Declare regional emergency. Suspend parliament. Assume air command.' Signed: RUSK, AIR MARSHAL.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Rusk. He gave the speech at Teal's wing ceremony. He told us the sky belongs to whoever is willing to be up in it.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Marines have the paper copy. Now the archive gives us his signature too. And the city still hears nothing but him.

transcript.speaker: RUSK
transcript.text: Citizens. Parliament has fled. Rebel aircraft are over the harbour. Stay inside. Trust the lights. Trust my voice.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: One tower, one voice, one emergency on repeat. He didn't build it to tell anyone anything. He built it so nothing else gets in.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The broadcast relay sits in a block of apartments. He chose that too. The canal is the only dark line through the city.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Everyone in those apartments has been listening to him for a year. I'd like to give them some quiet.

transcript.speaker: RUSK
transcript.text: Trainee. This is Rusk. Teal flew my wing the winter the coast starved while parliament debated. He had talent too. Ask the pass how far it got him.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: That's the first time he's used his own name. He wants you to know he's a person. Don't let him.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: He flew your wing. Vulture Lead hunted him for you. I'll remember who gave the order.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: A loyalist column is crossing the dry coast. Parliament is coming home by road. The ruined town ahead of them still has guns.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Don't fly for the people giving orders. Fly for the people who have to live beneath them. The man on the net is weather.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: He recorded that one at two in the morning. I can hear the hangar heater behind him. I could find that hangar in the dark by that sound.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Clear the bunkers ahead of the column. Stay on their channel until both squads answer from the streets.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Beneath them. Right. The road, then.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Recovery reached the upper pass this morning. They found his aircraft. They found him. He was in the seat. The recorder was still running.

transcript.speaker: RECORDER
transcript.text: RECORDER 7-T. ENTRY 04:12. PLAYBACK.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Two taps. Sparrow, it's me. Lead is on my tail and I'm out of altitude, so I'm going to stay in the pass a while. The seed trucks need ten minutes.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: I flew that order knowing the price. The tapes are so you never have to take my word for any of it. This part I'm choosing myself.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Fly the pattern too low and too fast. Nobody ever fixed it. Good. The sky will...

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Witnesses reach parliament tonight. Keep the bridges and quay open. Rusk leads four wingmen over the capital. Vulture Lead is one of them.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: I've amended the record myself. 'Aircraft lost with pilot. KILLED, NOT DESERTED.' Command can court-martial the paperwork.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Ten minutes. He bought ten minutes. I'm going to go and spend them.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The wing is broken. Rusk left his wingmen and ran to the coastal relay works. He's alone there with one relay and his own voice.

transcript.speaker: RUSK
transcript.text: Trainee. Land, and I'll tell the city you were misled by a dead man. Fly, and you're the traitor in every history I write.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: When you have the truth, send it in your own voice. You don't have to sound like me. You never did.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: I've got every harbour on the net. Every loyalist station is listening for one call sign. Not his. Yours.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Break the generators, run the vent and get clear. When his loop stops, he'll come up alone. Then the sky is yours to answer him.
